reason: Harvesting lettuce is the only available combination and should move me toward eating from the garden.
expectation: I expect to cut some fresh lettuce leaves, perhaps to prepare at the galley afterward.

effect: The harvest produced lettuce leaves, so I can take them to the galley to work toward the meal.
reaction: The result was expected; nothing else notable.
reason: Using the leaves at the galley is the clearest next step toward eating from the garden.
expectation: I expect to prepare or eat the lettuce with the available ration, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The meal completed the chapter and connected the surviving garden with the still-protected discovery in the ice.
reaction: The sound of the two fans made the quiet meal feel grounded in the work of keeping both alive and cold.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the supper was most worthwhile: the fresh leaves and the two fans brought the garden and the frozen discovery together in one quiet moment.

leastWorthwhile.text: Harvesting the lettuce was a predictable step with no additional detail in its result, though it made sense as preparation for the meal.

surprise.text: The supper passage brought the cold case into the scene through the sound of its fan, linking the meal to the discovery.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: cutting the lettuce and taking it to the galley both had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would continue to see what happens to the frozen discovery and how the station comes through the storm, though this chapter offered little decision-making on its own.
